command: fabio data-agent validate-fewshots --workspace $WS_ID --id $AGENT_ID --datasource MyLakehouse --llm-endpoint https://<resource>.openai.azure.com --llm-key $KEY --llm-model gpt-4o
description: Uses an external LLM judge to review a data source's few-shot examples and flag duplicates, semantic conflicts, ambiguity, low-quality examples, and likely-incorrect queries. Fabio hosts no model; the caller supplies the judge via --llm-endpoint/--llm-key/--llm-model (or FABIO_LLM_ENDPOINT/FABIO_LLM_KEY/FABIO_LLM_MODEL). Mirrors the Python SDK's few-shot validation.

data.summary: Contains a duplicated question mapped to conflicting queries and an incorrect SQL example.

issues.explanation: The first two examples are the same question but map to different SQL, which will confuse the model.
issues.suggestion: Keep a single canonical example (use SUM(revenue)).

issues.explanation: SELECT COUNT(*) does not answer 'total revenue' — it counts rows, not the sum.
issues.suggestion: Replace with SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM products.

notes: The LLM endpoint auto-detects flavor from the host: *.azure.com -> Azure OpenAI ({endpoint}/openai/deployments/{model}/chat/completions, api-key header); anything else -> OpenAI-compatible ({endpoint}/chat/completions, Bearer auth, model in body). For Azure, --llm-model is the DEPLOYMENT name (not the base model). Issue types: duplicate, conflict, ambiguous, low_quality, incorrect_query. --stage staging|published selects which config's few-shots to read. This is read-only: it does not modify the agent.

query_examples.description: How many issues the judge found (0 = clean).
